content: The SIX1 protein, also known as Sine oculis homeobox homolog 1, is a protein in humans encoded by the SIX1 gene. The vertebrate SIX genes are homologous to the Drosophila sine oculis (so) gene, which is predominantly expressed in the developing visual system of the fruit fly. Proteins encoded by members of the SIX gene family are characterized by a divergent DNA-binding homeodomain and an upstream SIX domain. The SIX domain is thought to play a role in determining DNA-binding specificity and mediating protein-protein interactions. Genes within the SIX family have been demonstrated to play critical roles in the development of vertebrates and insects. Additionally, they have been implicated in maintaining the differentiated state of tissues. The SIX1 protein has been shown to interact with several other proteins, including EYA1, DACH, GRO, and MDFI.
